title: Payroll system: what the contracts on disk say it cost
question: What did the school district agree to pay the firms that built and then propped up its payroll system?
finding: The implementation contract with Infosys, approved in October 2019 at $9.5 million, was raised three times in twelve months to $16,482,810 by June 2022 (+74%), each time to push go-live back or to stabilise the system after it went live. After the November 2022 emergency an audit team found about $4.3 million of overpayments in over 1,200 pay claims. A separate staffing agreement with Protiviti carried a $1.5 million cap for 2023-24 while its rate table priced 40 people full-time at $8.0 million; the 2024-25 agreement on disk leaves its price clause as template text, with $5 million on the budget-code line.
how: Ceilings and dates read from the amendment texts (each states the old and new ceiling); the Protiviti capacity is the rate table multiplied out (people x hourly rate x 40 hours x 49 weeks); the SAP order form was read by OCR.
limits: A ceiling is a maximum, not what was paid: the warrant registers that would show payments to Infosys and Protiviti are not on disk. A rate table lists the roles a firm may supply; the cap, not the table, limits the bill. A blank price clause on a posted copy may be a draft, with the signed copy held by the Procurement Department. Overpayments found are to be recovered from employees, not lost. Delaying go-live to finish testing is ordinary in large system projects.

rows.what: Board approves Infosys as implementation partner for the new payroll and personnel system (chosen by request for proposals)
First amendment: post-go-live support; term to 8 August 2022
Second amendment: go-live moved from July 2021 to January 2022; term to 17 February 2023
Third amendment: stabilisation support and extra capacity; term to 30 June 2023 (board slide prices the two parts at $1,460,556 and $1,288,434)
Superintendent declares a payroll state of emergency
Board update: a payroll audit team (district staff, Robert Half, Infosys, Alvarez & Marsal) audited over 1,200 pay claims, about $4.3 million of overpayments; ticket backlog had peaked at 10,514

Protiviti (Robert Half) staffing agreement for payroll, benefits and accounting roles, 2023-24: cap $1,500,000. Its rate table lists 40 people at $90-$135 an hour, 40 hours a week for 49 weeks, which would cost $8,036,000 if all were used
Protiviti agreement for 2024-25: the price clause still reads "INSERT DOLLAR AMOUNT"; the budget-code line beneath it carries $5,000,000

Signed top-up of SAP cloud licences (1,000 time-and-attendance users and others) from 3 March 2025 to 3 November 2026, a year after the board chose a replacement system and four months before it launched; board item 8 April 2025
